instruction_text: Speak directly to one listener with warmth and a smile in your voice; calm, steady and reassuring, like a favorite morning radio host, while keeping the news clear and credible.
asr_text: First thing every morning, I see the kids who come to the nurse's office. I'm sleepy, they say. My head hurts, they say. The other day, a student was resting on the bed. Their phone screen glowed beside the pillow. When I hear they stayed up until morning, I don't know what to say. I also think about one student. After their phone was taken away at school, they stopped coming to see me. If they don't come, does that mean they are okay? A teacher asked me, if we ban phones, will fewer kids come to the nurse's office? I could not answer. If the school bans phones during breaks too, will it think the problem is solved? That scares me. I don't take phones away in the nurse's office. I want to keep a place where kids can talk about what happened at night. After the phones are off limits, who will listen to that child?
